brief: Replacing an old or failing heat pump. When repair stops being worth it (compressor failure on an old unit, parts no longer made, old refrigerant, repeated faults). What a replacement involves: refrigerant recovery, removing both units, checking whether the old pipe route, drain, hole and electrical circuit can be reused, resizing rather than matching the old unit's kW. Old units that were oversized or undersized. Link to repair, sizing, installation cost and installation pages.

Heat pumps for Christchurch landlords and the Healthy Homes heating standard. The rule: one or more fixed qualifying heaters that can directly heat the main living room to at least 18°C, sized to the required heating capacity; a heat pump used for it must have a thermostat; open fires and unflued combustion heaters don't qualify; required capacity is worked out with the Tenancy Services heating assessment tool (link https://tools.tenancy.govt.nz/heating-tool) or the formula in the regulations. If the required capacity is over 2.4 kW the heater must be at least 2 kW. Newer homes (built to the 2008 code) use a different formula that usually gives a smaller figure. What we give landlords: the model and capacity in writing for their records. Rentals are common in Riccarton, Ilam, Upper Riccarton, Addington, Phillipstown. Do not state penalties or dates.

Ceiling cassette heat pumps: an indoor unit set into the ceiling with a grille that blows air out in several directions. Good where there's no wall space, in open plan rooms, kitchens and living areas, and where people don't want a box on the wall. Needs ceiling space above for the unit, pipes and a condensate drain (often with a pump), so it suits new builds and renovations or homes with roof space. Compare with high wall, floor console and ducted. Link to types of heat pumps, high wall, floor mounted, ducted pages. Brands we fit: Mitsubishi Electric, Daikin, Fujitsu and Toshiba.

How to read a fault on a Mitsubishi Electric heat pump: flashing operation light, how to check the code with the remote (self-diagnosis), what to note (model number, code, what the unit was doing). Do NOT list specific code numbers or what each one means: codes vary by model and we can't verify them. Explain common causes in general terms (sensor, fan motor, communication between indoor and outdoor unit, refrigerant, drain), what the owner can safely check (filters, isolating switch reset, outdoor unit clear), and when to call us. Link to mitsubishi-heat-pump-service-christchurch, heat-pump-repair, heat-pump-troubleshooting.

Same as the Mitsubishi guide but for Daikin: flashing light, checking the code with the remote, what to note. Do NOT list specific code numbers or meanings. Write it differently from the Mitsubishi page: no shared sentences.

Same idea for Fujitsu: flashing timer and operation lights, reading the code, what to note. Do NOT list specific code numbers or meanings. General causes, safe owner checks, when to call us. secondary: how much does a heat pump cost to run
brief: What decides a heat pump's running cost in Christchurch: size match to the room, insulation and draughts, set temperature (around 18 to 21°C), using auto fan, leaving it on low versus switching off and on, clean filters and coil, frosty mornings and defrost, the unit's efficiency rating. Best winter settings. Do NOT give dollar figures, kWh figures or percentages: tell the reader to work it out from the unit's rated input power and their own power price per kWh, with a worked method in words. Link to energy-consumption-monitoring, maintenance-servicing, heat-pump-sizing, energy-star-heat-pumps.

secondary: heat pump or wood burner christchurch
brief: Comparing a heat pump with a wood burner and with gas heating for a Christchurch home: how each heats (spread, speed, control, cooling in summer), fuel and upkeep (buying and storing wood, chimney sweeping, gas bottles or connection), air quality and Christchurch's rules on burners (building consent needed to install or move a solid fuel burner; new burners since 1 January 2019 must be ultra-low emission; fixed electric heaters including heat pumps don't need building consent, an electrician connects them). No running cost figures or percentages. Many homes keep a burner and add a heat pump. Link to heat-pump-carbon-footprint-analysis, heat-pump-installation-in-christchurch, heat-pump-sizing.
